newsitem.title: USA: Variflex cites excess inventory at retail.
newsitem.headline: Variflex cites excess inventory at retail.

text.p: Variflex Inc said Friday it had a loss in the fourth quarter, ended July 31, adding this was primarily due to excess retail inventory.

The company said it expects to report a loss of between $1.1 million and $1.3 million, or $0.18 to $0.21 per share, on sales of about $13 million for the quarter and net income of between $500,000 and $700,000, or $0.08 to $0.11 per share, on sales of about $72 million for the year ended July 31.
The First Call consensus estimate prior to Variflex's announcement projected the company would earn $0.07 per share in the latest quarter, giving it annual earnings of $0.36.

In the final quarter fiscal 1995, Variflex earned $546,000, or $0.09 per share, on sales of $18.5 million. For all of 1995, it reported earnings of $6,921,000, or $1.15 per share, on sales of $100.3 million.

"Our fourth quarter results reflect significant markdown credits and returns to help several of our customers make way for our new models on their shelves," President Jay Losi said without providing any specifics.
"Additionally, we had closeout sales and writedowns relating to excess inventory in-house," Losi said.
He did say the fourth quarter would have been "roughly breakeven" if not for these issues.

"Our relationships with our major retail customers are vital. This has been a difficult year for some of them, and we felt we had to do what we could to help them reduce their inventories and clear the way for more new orders," Losi said.
"I am confident that the coming year will be stronger than fiscal 1996 as a result of several" recent events, he added.

"Our joint manufacturing and marketing agreement with Barfoot Snoboards will bring a lot of recognition to our Static Snowboard operations and gives us a world-renowned brand name for the specialty market.

"Also, our new opening in-line skate order for Wal-Mart (Stores Inc ) will ship in time for the holiday season. And we continue to reap the benefit of a resurgence in skateboards, where Variflex is still the best known name in the marketplace," Losi explained.
